conventions.convention: L has entries ∂u_i/∂x_j; D=(L+Lᵀ)/2; incompressibility means tr L=0. Tensor contraction and norm are the Frobenius product S:T=tr(SᵀT) and |S|²=S:S.
The shear-rate scalar is √(2D:D). The Bingham yield parameter is the radius of the trace-free symmetric Frobenius stress ball at zero strain rate.

Positive-base real powers use exp(r log_nat a), evaluated on numerical values in fixed SI units. The unregularized power viscosity is evaluated only at positive shear rate; its stress is extended by zero at D=0.
Conformation evolves in symmetric matrices; stored energy is defined only on positive-definite matrices, using log r=∫₁ʳ ds/s. G and λ are strictly positive; solvent viscosity is nonnegative.

Conformation positivity is asserted forward from positive-definite initial data at time zero on [0,T], with one-sided endpoint derivatives. No backward positivity, PDE existence, or entropy-production conclusion is asserted.
Rigid observer changes preserve time and have x*=Q(t)x+c(t), Q∈SO(3), with Q,c of class C²; objective second-order tensors transform by orthogonal conjugation.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the incompressible generalized Newtonian law τ=2η(√(2D:D))D, the trace-free Frobenius Bingham graph, and the symmetric conformation equation D_tC−LC−CLᵀ=−(C−I₃)/λ with τ_p=G(C−I₃), τ_s=2η_sD, and w(C)=G(tr C−log det C−3)/2 on positive-definite C.

Under the stated C¹ incompressible trajectory hypotheses, symmetric conformation evolution with C(0)>0, G,λ>0 and η_s≥0 preserves positive definiteness on [0,T]; w≥0 with equality exactly at C=I₃; and (τ_s+τ_p):D−w′=2η_sD:D+G(tr C+tr C⁻¹−6)/(2λ)≥0. The equation is covariant under the stated rigid observer changes, stresses transform by conjugation, and w is invariant.

For μ_p,τ_y≥0 on trace-free symmetric matrices with the Frobenius product, Φ(D)=μ_p|D|²+τ_y|D| is finite, nonnegative and convex; B(D)=∂Φ(D); the graph is monotone, every graph value satisfies τ:D≥0, and B(QDQᵀ)=QB(D)Qᵀ for Q∈SO(3).

For a C² incompressible motion and finite continuous η:[0,∞)→[0,∞), τ=2η(√(2D:D))D satisfies τ:D≥0 and transforms objectively under the stated C² rigid observer changes. The stated Carreau and regularized power formulas are finite and nonnegative under their parameter hypotheses; for m,n>0 the unregularized power stress has a continuous zero extension.

published_dependencies.used_for: Positive-base real-power definition used in the constitutive formulas.
Continuity and differentiation of positive-base powers in viscosity monotonicity and limiting arguments.
Exponent identities in the zero-rate stress limit and Carreau asymptotics.
Strict monotonicity of positive powers from their derivative signs.
Positivity and reciprocal identities for real powers and conformation integrating factors.
Orthonormal diagonalization of symmetric conformation matrices.
Positive determinant, eigenvalue-product formula, and invariance under orthogonal conjugation.
Existence of Z′=LZ, Z(0)=I₃ on the compact interval [0,T] for continuous L.
Differentiation of Z⁻¹ in the positivity argument.
Composition of matrix derivatives with differentiable paths.
Entrywise product differentiation for finite matrix products.
Differentiating det C in the stored-energy identity.
Identification of the integral logarithm with the natural logarithm and its derivative 1/r.
Expansion of log det C as the sum of logarithms of positive eigenvalues.
Positive square roots and inverse square roots in the spectral nonnegativity calculation.

concerns.concern: Proof step 4.1 says 'the fundamental theorem of calculus gives' the integral representation of Y, but no fundamental-theorem supplier is declared in deps or Facts & Assumptions. The application is valid entrywise because Y is C¹ and its displayed derivative is continuous; this is a small missing prerequisite/citation rather than a defect in the positivity conclusion.

seams_checked.note: Checked the smooth-motion definition and observer-calculus lemma. The motion, Eulerian velocity, gradient convention, and rigid-observer strain transformation are preserved. The conformation lemma's more general trajectory formulation also verifies covariance directly by differentiation.

Read the adopted-model definition and conditional-admissibility theorem. They preserve the Frobenius yield normalization, viscosity parameter ranges, conformation equation, positive initial data, forward-time interval, and dissipation identity. Entropy production requires separately stated isothermal energy, Helmholtz, and thermostat assumptions; empirical applicability and PDE existence are expressly excluded.
